correctness.rationale: The fixed-Kendall equation is solved exactly, yielding beta=t alpha/[alpha(1+t)-t]. Substitution into the published directional Chatterjee formula gives Xi_t(alpha)=2t alpha^2/[alpha(t+3)-2t]. Its derivative has the unique zero 4t/(t+3), and endpoint limits give the exact interval. Direct factorization of the difference between forward and reverse Chatterjee coefficients proves the orientation sign rule. Tail reconstruction is exact algebra.

value.rationale: The theorem gives sharp calibration limits for a classical asymmetric dependence model and resolves an identifiability question: Kendall and Spearman collapse to one degree of information, while directional Chatterjee correlation retains asymmetry. The weak-dependence gap is substantial, with compatible xi values ranging from order t^2 to order t, so the distinction matters quantitatively rather than only parametrically.
